name: JavaScript Obfuscation & Deobfuscation — Techniques and Tools
description: JavaScript obfuscation techniques and deobfuscation workflow. Obfuscation types: (1) Minification — single long line (.min.js), (2) Packing — eval(function(p,a,c,k,e,d){...}) pattern, recognizable by 6-arg function, (3) Advanced — obfuscator.io with Base64 string arrays, (4) JSFuck/JJEncode/AAEncode — bracket-only or Unicode encoding. Deobfuscation: Browser DevTools Pretty Print ({}), Beautifier.io, Prettier.io, UnPacker (matthewfl.com). Packed code: find return value, replace eval with console.log. Source discovery: Ctrl+U (view-source), CTRL+SHIFT+Z (Firefox debugger), check <script src='...'> tags.
notes:
=== FINDING JAVASCRIPT SOURCE ===
In browser:
  Ctrl+U → view-source:http://TARGET:PORT (view raw HTML)
  Ctrl+Shift+Z (Firefox) or Ctrl+Shift+I (Chrome) → DevTools
  F12 → Sources/Debugger tab → find .js files

In HTML source, JS can be:
  Internal:  <script>console.log('...')</script>
  External:  <script src="secret.js"></script>
             → fetch via: curl http://TARGET:PORT/secret.js

Always check HTML comments for sensitive info!
  <!-- TODO: remove this API key: sk-abc123 -->

=== OBFUSCATION TYPES ===

--- Type 1: Minification ---
All code on a single line; removes whitespace/newlines.
Saved as .min.js
Example:
  var a=1;function b(){console.log(a);}b();
Deobfuscate with: Prettier, Beautifier (format only, no hidden logic)

--- Type 2: Packing ---
Recognizable pattern: eval(function(p,a,c,k,e,d){...})
The 6 arguments (p,a,c,k,e,d) are the giveaway
Code builds a word dictionary and reconstructs at runtime
Strings MAY still be visible inside the packed code (less secure)

Example packer output:
  eval(function(p,a,c,k,e,d){e=function(c){return c};
  ...}('5.4(\'3 2 1 0\');',6,6,
  'Module|Deobfuscation|JavaScript|HTB|log|console'.split('|'),0,{}))

Deobfuscate:
  → UnPacker: https://matthewfl.com/unPacker.html
  → Or find the return statement in eval() and replace eval with console.log
  → Run in browser console (JSConsole): https://jsconsole.com

--- Type 3: Advanced (obfuscator.io) ---
Features: string array encoding (Base64/RC4), dead code, control flow flattening
No readable strings in output — all via encoded string array + lookup functions
Variable names changed to _0x prefixed hex values

Example snippet:
  var _0x1ec6=['Bg9N','sfrciePH...'];
  ...
  console[_0x14f8('0x0')](_0x14f8('0x1'));

Deobfuscate:
  → Harder to automate; browser devtools debugging
  → Set breakpoints around string decode functions
  → Some online tools: https://deobfuscate.relative.im/

--- Type 4: JSFuck / JJEncode / AAEncode ---
Extreme encoding — only uses 6 chars: []()!+
Generates massive code that runs correctly but is unreadable
Slow to execute (CPU-intensive to decode at runtime)
Not often used in real malware (too slow for large payloads)

JSFuck example prefix:
  [][(![]+[])[+[]]+([![]]+[][[]])[+!+[]+[+[]]]+...

Deobfuscate: run in browser console; result is readable JS

=== DEOBFUSCATION TOOLS ===

Browser DevTools Pretty Print:
  Firefox: CTRL+SHIFT+Z → Debugger → click script → click '{ }' button
  Chrome:  F12 → Sources → click script → click '{ }' at bottom
  → Only formats minified code; doesn't deobfuscate packing

Online tools:
  Beautifier.io:  https://beautifier.io/
  Prettier:       https://prettier.io/playground/
  UnPacker:       https://matthewfl.com/unPacker.html  ← best for packed code
  JS Nice:        https://jsnice.org/ (rename variables)
  de4js:          https://de4js.kshift.me/
  deobfuscate.io: https://deobfuscate.relative.im/

Manual trick for packed code:
  → Find the return p; at end of eval()
  → Replace eval( with console.log(
  → Run in JSConsole → prints the unpacked code without executing

=== CODE ANALYSIS AFTER DEOBFUSCATION ===
Deobfuscated secret.js:
  function generateSerial() {
    var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest;
    var url = '/serial.php';
    xhr.open('POST', url, true);
    xhr.send(null);
  }

XMLHttpRequest = JavaScript object for making HTTP requests
  → xhr.open('POST', url, true)  → method, URL, async=true
  → xhr.send(null)               → sends POST with no body
  → This function POSTs to /serial.php

=== REPLICATING JS FUNCTIONS WITH CURL ===
Emulate the JS function from command line:

Simple GET:
  curl http://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/

POST with no data (replicating xhr.send(null)):
  curl -s http://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/serial.php -X POST

POST with data:
  curl -s http://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/serial.php -X POST -d 'param1=sample'

POST with decoded serial:
  curl -s http://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/serial.php -X POST -d 'serial=DECODED_VALUE'

  -s = silent (suppress progress meter)
  -X POST = HTTP method
  -d = data body (URL-encoded by default)

=== WORKFLOW SUMMARY ===
1. View HTML source (Ctrl+U)
2. Find <script src='...'> → fetch file
3. Identify obfuscation type (packer? minified? JSFuck?)
4. Use appropriate deobfuscation tool
5. Read/analyze the deobfuscated code
6. Identify HTTP requests, API calls, encoded strings
7. Decode any encoded values (base64/hex/rot13)
8. Replicate the function with curl
